42887436.label: Objectives
42887436.text: Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS) is a severe obstetric complication. This study evaluated whether retrospective, post-processing deep learning-based super-resolution reconstruction (SR) was associated with improved MRI radiomics performance for predicting PAS and invasive PAS.

42887436.label: Materials & methods
42887436.text: This retrospective study involved 245 patients who had placental MRI scans at three different institutions. Of these, 158 cases from Institution I for training set and internal validation set, while 34 patients from Institution II and 53 patients from Institution III served as external validation sets. SR using a generative adversarial network (GAN) was applied to generate SR T2WI (SRT2WI). Predictive models for PAS and invasive PAS were developed based on T2WI, SRT2WI, and the SRT2WI-Clinical model. Two radiologists independently diagnosed PAS using T2WI to serve as a reference for evaluating model performance. Model performance was assessed using the area under the curve (AUC), calibration curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), Delong test, and net reclassification improvement (NRI). SHAP values interpreted the models and quantified feature contributions.

42887436.label: Results
42887436.text: Across all four cohorts, SRT2WI yielded numerically higher AUCs than T2WI, and SRT2WI-Clinical achieved the highest AUCs. For PAS, SRT2WI-Clinical achieved AUCs of 0.953, 0.887, 0.793, and 0.788 in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts 1 and 2, respectively (T2WI: 0.738, 0.697, 0.654, and 0.652; SRT2WI: 0.879, 0.820, 0.696, and 0.768). Corresponding AUCs for invasive PAS were 0.895, 0.875, 0.843, and 0.815 (T2WI: 0.774, 0.699, 0.575, and 0.745; SRT2WI: 0.861, 0.794, 0.729, and 0.808). For PAS, SRT2WI-Clinical significantly outperformed T2WI (P < 0.001) and SRT2WI (P = 0.004) only in training, with no significant validation differences. For invasive PAS, it significantly outperformed T2WI in training, internal validation, and external validation cohort 1 (P = 0.003, 0.021, and 0.019, respectively), but not external validation cohort 2 (P = 0.398); comparisons with SRT2WI were nonsignificant. Calibration showed good agreement, DCA favored SRT2WI-Clinical, and SHAP quantified feature contributions.

42887436.label: Conclusions
42887436.text: The combination of SR and radiomics shows promise for improving the prediction of PAS and invasive PAS. Integrating clinical features may further enhance model performance, supporting its potential clinical utility.

42899936.text: Background Poor outcome after successful endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) may reflect microvascular dysfunction, or no-reflow phenomenon, but operational definitions are lacking. Purpose To identify the most informative candidate no-reflow definition at 24-hour post-EVT perfusion imaging for outcome assessment. Materials and Methods This secondary analysis used data from two prospective multicenter imaging registries of patients with acute stroke who were recruited between June 2016 and July 2022, achieved modified thrombolysis in cerebral infarction grade 2c or 3 recanalization after EVT, and underwent pre-EVT and 24-hour post-EVT CT or MR perfusion imaging. Candidate no-reflow definitions were evaluated across eight perfusion maps and their corresponding stepwise thresholds. Delay time (DT) quantifies the delay in contrast material arrival between arterial input and brain tissue. For primary screening, no-reflow status was defined as any residual hypoperfusion lesion for each map-threshold combination. The best-performing combination was evaluated using residual volume and reperfusion index cutoffs. The primary outcome was poor 90-day functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score >2); infarct growth was secondary. Associations with the outcome were evaluated using multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression. Results The primary cohort included 67 patients (median age, 69 years [IQR, 56-77 years]; 41 male), and the independent cohort comprised 54 patients (median age, 69 years [IQR, 62-78 years]; 28 female). In the primary cohort, lesions with DT longer than 4 seconds showed the strongest discrimination for poor 90-day functional outcome (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.72 [95% CI: 0.57, 0.86]; P < .001). According to this definition, 14 of 67 patients (21%) had no reflow. Poor functional outcome occurred in 11 of 14 patients (79%) with no reflow and 11 of 53 (21%) with reflow (odds ratio, 12.14 [95% CI: 3.38, 54.63]; P < .001). Infarct growth was greater with no-reflow status than with reflow (median, 24.1 mL [IQR, 3.7-40.7 mL] vs 0 mL [IQR, -10.1 to 6.1 mL]; P < .001). Findings were consistent in the independent cohort. Conclusion The presence of a lesion with DT longer than 4 seconds at 24-hour post-EVT perfusion imaging appeared to be the most informative candidate no-reflow definition.

42937536.text: Background Low-dose CT (LDCT) for lung cancer screening enables opportunistic volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD) assessment, but its prognostic value is unclear. Purpose To evaluate fully automated LDCT-derived vBMD for predicting vertebral fractures and its association with mortality in individuals who heavily smoke. Materials and Methods This secondary analysis included 55-74-year-old individuals who heavily smoked (≥30 pack-years) from the CT arm of the National Lung Screening Trial (NLST), a multicenter randomized controlled trial of LDCT versus radiography (participants recruited August 2002 to April 2004). Automated SpineQ software (Bonescreen) was used to measure thoracic and lumbar vBMD (normal, ≥120 mg/cm3; low bone mass [osteopenia], 80 to <120 mg/cm3; osteoporosis, <80 mg/cm3) and vertebral fractures (Genant scale). The outcomes included 1- and 2-year incident vertebral fractures and 6-year mortality (active follow-up to 2009). Poisson and Cox models were adjusted for demographic variables, available comorbidities, and baseline vertebral fractures. Results The NLST included 26 722 participants in the CT arm, with 21 856 included in the present analysis (mean age, 61 years ± 5 [SD]; 12 854 male participants). The 2-year vertebral fracture incidence (n = 18 211 participants with 2-year LDCT) was 0.9% for those with normal bone mass, 2.0% for those with low bone mass (adjusted relative risk, 2.07 [95% CI: 1.70, 2.53]), and 5.9% for those with osteoporosis (adjusted relative risk, 3.40 [95% CI: 2.69, 4.30]). Mortality risk (n = 21 447 participants with completed follow-up [median, 6.65 years]) was associated with osteoporotic vBMD in men (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.24 [95% CI: 1.02, 1.50]). Conclusion Fully automated opportunistic assessment of spinal vBMD predicted vertebral fracture risk and was associated with mortality in men after adjustment. Individuals with osteoporotic vBMD who heavily smoked had a 2-year fracture incidence above the 5% treatment threshold according to current osteoporosis guidelines.

42954786.text: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a progressive disease associated with high morbidity and mortality. PH is classified into five groups based on underlying pathophysiology and etiology: pulmonary arterial hypertension (group 1); PH due to left heart disease (group 2); PH secondary to lung disease (group 3); pulmonary artery obstruction, including chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) (group 4); and PH due to unclear or multifactorial mechanisms (group 5). Radiologists play a major role in the multidisciplinary evaluation of patients with PH alongside specialists in pathology, pulmonary medicine, and cardiology. Given the widespread use of CT, imaging may be the first modality to suggest PH and plays a central role in the diagnosis and management of CTEPH. This review describes the pathophysiology of the five PH groups and emphasizes imaging findings that raise suspicion for PH. Discussion includes the roles of CT and MRI in PH evaluation, risk stratification, and assessment of treatment response, as well as the current applications of multienergy CT, echocardiography, and cardiac MRI in PH management.

42955836.text: Meckel diverticulum is the most common congenital anomaly of the gastrointestinal tract, yet it is frequently asymptomatic. Meckel diverticulum poses unique diagnostic challenges due to its variable manifestation and infrequent visualization at imaging. The authors review the embryology and anatomy of Meckel diverticulum, its normal radiologic appearances, and its complications and their management. Complications of Meckel diverticulum occur in up to 4%-9% of patients. Symptomatic Meckel diverticulum is more common in children but can also be seen in adults. A giant Meckel diverticulum, presence of ectopic gastric or pancreatic tissue, or adjacent adhesions and bands are associated with a higher likelihood of a symptomatic manifestation. The most common complications include small-bowel obstruction, gastrointestinal bleeding, and diverticulitis. Children more commonly present with gastrointestinal bleeding, while diverticulitis is more common in adults. Small-bowel obstruction can occur at any age and can be secondary to inversion of Meckel diverticulum, intussusception, volvulus, internal or external hernias, neoplasms, enteroliths, congenital bands, or postinflammatory changes. When a patient presents with acute abdomen or gastrointestinal bleeding, the choice of imaging modalities includes CT or US, with the latter preferred in the pediatric population. Technetium 99m-pertechnetate scintigraphy (Meckel scan) can be additionally performed to evaluate rectal bleeding in younger patients. MRI is reserved as a problem-solving tool. Meckel diverticulum should be differentiated from its common imaging mimics (eg, the appendix, ileal duplication cyst, and mesenteric small-bowel diverticulum). When Meckel diverticulum is not visualized at imaging, the radiologist still plays a key role by raising suspicion for an underlying Meckel diverticulum and identifying other critical imaging findings that can inform clinical management. An understanding of the common clinical manifestations associated with Meckel diverticulum and a systematic imaging approach can improve preoperative diagnosis and patient management.

43000586.label: Background
43000586.text: Bone metastases frequently occur in advanced-stage malignancies, contributing to diminished quality of life and unfavorable prognoses. However, conventional imaging modalities for diagnosing bone metastases exhibit inherent limitations. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic utility of fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) imaging using [99mTc]Tc-H7ND for detecting bone metastases (BM). From June 2021 to September 2023, 564 patients with malignancies underwent FAPI imaging were screened. Eighty patients with confirmed or suspected BM were included. FAPI SPECT/CT was compared with CT, MRI, bone scintigraphy (BS), and [¹⁸F]FDG PET/CT for diagnostic efficacy. The uptake values in different components of BM were assessed, alongside discussions on potential of FAPI imaging in evaluating treatment response.

43000586.label: Results
43000586.text: Eighty patients (median age: 60 years; range: 23-79 years; 48 men) with confirmed or suspected BM were included, of these, 64 were confirmed BM. FAPI SPECT/CT demonstrated superior sensitivity (96.5%) and accuracy (95.9%) compared to CT (59.7%, 67.1%; p < 0.001), detecting significantly more lesions than CT (p < 0.001) and MRI (p = 0.041). FAPI imaging outperformed BS in detecting osteolytic and mixed metastases, identifying 12 and 9 additional lesions, respectively. FAPI uptake differed significantly among BM subtypes, with median SUVmax values of 13.41 (osteolytic), 10.78 (mixed), and 2.70 (osteoblastic) (p < 0.001). Compared to conventional imaging combinations, FAPI identified new lesions in 46.3% of patients, prompting treatment modifications in 86.5% of cases. For patients who underwent follow-up FAPI imaging, changes in SUVmax of BM correlated with RECIST 1.1 criteria.

43000586.label: Conclusion
43000586.text: The findings may enhance diagnostic performance in detecting BM across malignancies, particularly for osteolytic and mixed metastases. Preliminary observations also suggest possible applications in monitoring therapeutic response, though further validation is required to confirm these exploratory findings. This is a retrospective study, utilizing data collected from a registry.

43019586.text: A gouty tophus found in the scapula is exceedingly rare. Here, we report on a 62-year-old asymptomatic woman with no history of gout or hyperuricemia who was incidentally found on chest CT screening to have a localized osteolytic lesion in the left scapula. 18F-FDG PET/CT demonstrated abnormally increased FDG uptake within this lesion, concerning for a neoplasm. Subsequent biopsy confirmed a gouty tophus, a rare mimic of malignancy in this location.

43051336.label: Background
43051336.text: Pulmonary nodules may be missed on chest radiographs despite their clinical relevance for early lung cancer detection. Commercial artificial intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly available for chest radiograph interpretation, but evidence for their standalone performance remains fragmented across products, datasets, operating thresholds, and comparator designs.

43051336.label: Purpose
43051336.text: To systematically evaluate the standalone diagnostic performance of commercially available AI software for pulmonary nodule detection on chest radiographs compared with radiologists reading alone, and to identify methodological factors shaping interpretation of the evidence.

43051336.label: Methods
43051336.text: PubMed, PubMed Central, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched. Eligible studies evaluated commercially available AI systems as standalone detectors for pulmonary nodules on chest radiographs and directly compared their performance with radiologists reading alone using an accepted clinical reference standard. Risk of bias was assessed using an adapted QUADAS-2 framework. Findings were synthesized narratively because of heterogeneity in study design, populations, reference standards, operating thresholds, and outcome measures.

43051336.label: Results
43051336.text: Six studies met the inclusion criteria, comprising 12 product-level evaluations across 10 commercial AI systems. Standalone AI performance varied: some evaluations showed AI exceeding radiologist-level performance, others showed no significant difference, and one showed AI below individual reader performance with approximately twice the false-positive rate. In the only standardized within-study comparison of multiple commercial products on the same dataset, four of seven systems significantly exceeded mean radiologist AUC. Standalone AI AUC ranged from 0.79 to 0.93 against a mean reader AUC of 0.81 (95% CI 0.77-0.85), indicating that performance varied among cleared products even when tested under identical conditions. Interpretation was limited by differences in operating thresholds, comparator design, reference standards, study populations, and outcome reporting. Risk-of-bias concerns were common, particularly in patient selection.

43051336.label: Conclusions
43051336.text: In the available peer-reviewed evidence, standalone commercial AI systems for chest radiograph pulmonary nodule detection show variable performance. Evidence remains insufficient to support class-wide standalone deployment because all studies were retrospective or reader-study based, thresholds were inconsistently reported, and real-world false-positive burden remains uncertain. Prospective real world evaluation with clearly reported operating thresholds, standardized comparator designs and complete diagnostic performance are needed.

43064186.label: Background
43064186.text: Quantitative myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) requires tracers with high myocardial extraction fraction (EF) and favorable kinetic properties. Although 99mTc-4BOH has demonstrated favorable myocardial imaging characteristics, its myocardial extraction behavior and the factors that may influence EF in the circulation have not been fully characterized.

43064186.label: Methods
43064186.text: Myocardial EF and retention kinetics of 99mTc-4BOH were evaluated using isolated Langendorff-perfused rat hearts across low-, intermediate-, and high-flow conditions (5.0, 8.4, and 16.0 mL/min) and compared with 99mTc-Teboroxime and 99mTc-Sestamibi. Time-dependent changes in myocardial EF were assessed at 2, 4, and 10 min after tracer administration in vivo. Potential blood-related mechanisms were investigated by in vitro incubation with whole blood, plasma, and erythrocytes at the same time points.

43064186.label: Results
43064186.text: 99mTc-4BOH demonstrated a high and flow-independent myocardial EF across the tested flow rates (mean values, 96.5%-99.5%), comparable to 99mTc-Teboroxime and consistently higher than 99mTc-Sestamibi at each flow rate. Despite similarly high extraction, 99mTc-4BOH exhibited greater myocardial retention than 99mTc-Teboroxime. Following in vivo circulation, myocardial EF progressively declined to approximately 84% at 2 min and 57% at 10 min. In vitro incubation with whole blood or plasma had minimal effects on EF, whereas erythrocyte-associated tracer exhibited a time-dependent decline from approximately 92% at 2 min to 59% at 10 min, suggesting that erythrocyte interaction contributes to, but does not fully explain, the loss of EF observed after circulation.

43064186.label: Conclusion
43064186.text: 99mTc-4BOH exhibits near-complete, flow-independent myocardial EF and greater retention than 99mTc-Teboroxime, supporting its potential as a tracer for quantitative SPECT MPI. The time-dependent decline in EF following circulation has important implications for kinetic modeling and suggests that early post-injection imaging data may be preferable for myocardial blood flow quantification.
